qt: to the Commission Magdalena Adamowicz (PPE), Marta Wcisło (PPE), Mirosława Nykiel (PPE), Regina Doherty (PPE), Isabel Wiseler-Lima (PPE), Jagna Marczułajtis-Walczak (PPE), Caterina Chinnici (PPE), Kamila Gasiuk-Pihowicz (PPE), Ewa Kopacz (PPE), Zala Černilec Tomašič (PPE), Elżbieta Katarzyna Łukacijewska (PPE), Maria Guzenina (S&D) Subject:

Sexual exploitation of children in travel and tourism keeps growing and changing shape. Volunteer tourism and orphanage tourism put travellers in direct, often unsupervised contact with children; ECPAT, a global network focused on ending the sexual exploitation of children, has documented how demand from paying volunteers drives the recruitment of children into institutions. The provisional agreement of 22 June 2026 between Parliament and the Council on the recast of the Child Sexual Abuse Directive1 extends limitation periods and requires criminal record checks for professional and organised voluntary work involving regular contact with children. These duties stop at the EU’s borders. Beyond them, extraterritorial prosecution is still blocked by double criminality requirements (in a survey, ECPAT found that only 7 out of 44 countries had dropped them), and victims have no realistic route to compensation. In the light of the above: 1.
How will the Commission ensure that criminal record checks reach EU-based organisations placing volunteers with children in non-EU countries?
What will the Commission do, through its external action and development instruments, to remove double criminality as an obstacle to prosecuting EU nationals for abuse committed abroad?
Will the Commission assess whether victims in non-EU countries can obtain compensation when the offender is an EU national?

Directive 2011/93/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 December 2011 on combating the sexual abuse and sexual exploitation of children and child pornography, and replacing Council Framework Decision 2004/68/JHA (OJ L 335, 17.12.2011, p. 1, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/dir/2011/93/oj). 1
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (6.11.2026) The provisional agreement on the proposal for a recast of the Child Sexual Abuse Directive1 strengthens safeguards to prevent reoffending. Member States must ensure that a person convicted of offences under the Directive can be barred from professional and organised voluntary activities involving direct and regular contact with children. Employers recruiting for such activities will in future be required to request information on relevant convictions or disqualifications. These provisions apply to EU-based organisations recruiting volunteers in the EU for direct and regular contact with children in third countries. The criminal background of EU nationals can be verified through the European Criminal Records Information System (ECRIS). The 2027 expansion of ECRIS will allow requestors to identify Member States that hold information on previous convictions of third-country nationals and stateless persons. The recast also strengthens extraterritorial prosecution. Jurisdiction over certain offences committed abroad by nationals of a Member State no longer depends on the conduct also being criminalised in the country where it occurred. The Victims’ Rights Directive2 confers rights on victims of extra-territorial offences only in relation to criminal proceedings that take place in the EU. In accordance with national law, the agreement on the recast of the Child Sexual Abuse Directive ensures that victims – regardless of nationality – have the right to claim full compensation from offenders for damages resulting from any offence under the Directive. This applies across the offences listed in the Directive and therefore also covers victims of abuse linked to conduct committed abroad where national jurisdiction is established under the Directive.
1 Proposal for a Directive of the European Parliament and of the Council on combating the sexual abuse and

sexual exploitation of children and child sexual abuse material and replacing Council Framework Decision 2004/68/JHA (recast), COM/2024/60 final; https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legalcontent/EN/TXT/?uri=celex:52024PC0060. 2 Directive 2012/29/EU establishing minimum standards on the rights, support and protection of victims of crime, recently amended by Directive 2026/1472, OJ L, 2026/1472, 30.6.2026, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/dir/2026/1472/oj.
